resources.string: Also Apple Home and Alexa — through Matter, no Home Assistant or cloud needed

Add the car to Google Home: switch the climate on and off in the Google Home app or by voice, and the lights if you like. The bridge speaks Matter, the standard Google Home uses for local devices. You need a Google speaker, display or TV box at home.
Update the bridge to add the car to Google Home (Settings → Updates).
The bridge can\'t run this yet: update the bridge (Settings → Updates). It installs what it needs (Node.js) by itself.
IPv6 is switched off on the bridge computer, and Matter needs it.
1 · Once: let Google Home accept the bridge

Google Home only adds Matter devices it knows about. Register PHEV Link once, signed in with the same Google account as your Google Home:
1. Open the Google Home Developer Console and create a project (any name).
2. Choose “Add Matter integration”, then “Next: Setup”.
3. Product name: PHEV Link. Device type: the closest one, e.g. Outlet.
4. Vendor ID: 0xFFF1 (the test vendor). Product ID: 0x8000.
5. Save & continue. That's all — nothing is published.
In the Google Home app: Devices → Add → Matter-enabled device, and scan this code (or enter the numbers). When Google says the device isn\'t certified, continue.
Waiting for Google Home to add it…
Try “Hey Google, turn on %1$s”. You can rename the switches and put them in a room in the Google Home app.
While the car is away from home, its switches show as offline.
Changing this restarts the link for a moment; Google Home updates by itself (or say “Hey Google, sync my devices”).
In the Google Home app open the car\'s device → Settings → Linked Matter apps & services → Link apps & services. It shows a new code: scan it in the other app.
Remove the car from Google Home and every other app? You can add it again with a new code.
Removed — add it again with the new code.
